title: Fluorimetric microplate assay for alkaline phosphatase kinetics in activated sludge
author: Fischer, Wacht
materials: calibration standards without inhibitor addition; wells 7-
calibration standards containing inhibitor concentration “Y”, wells 7-

steps.title: Collect and store sludge sample
steps.instruction: Sample activated sludge from an aerated tank using a pre‑cleaned HDPE canister, transport to the laboratory, and if not used immediately store refrigerated; if storage exceeds several hours, keep aerated and supply nutrients. Wear protective equipment, vaccinate against hepatitis B, and clean benches with biocidal solution (e.g., ethanol).

steps.title: Resuspend sludge
steps.instruction: Immediately before use, place the sludge in an end‑over‑end shaker (or similar) and agitate for 5 min.

steps.title: Take subsample for treatment
steps.instruction: Pipette 50 mL of the resuspended sludge into a screw‑cap tube.

steps.title: Ultrasonic dispersion
steps.instruction: Insert the tube into an ultrasonic bath and treat for 10 min at 70 % of the maximum energy output to disperse flocs without lysing cells. Verify optimal conditions by measuring dehydrogenase activity (intracellular) while varying sonication time and power; choose the setting that gives maximal APA activity with minimal DHA activity.

steps.title: Dilute dispersed sludge
steps.instruction: Dilute an aliquot of the sonicated sludge with HEPES buffer; typical dilution ratios are 1:5 to 1:10. For example, to obtain 100 µL of a 1:5 diluted sample per well of a 96‑well plate, add 1.92 mL of the original sludge suspension to the required volume of HEPES.

steps.title: Select substrate concentrations
steps.instruction: Choose 12 different 4‑MUF‑phosphate concentrations ranging from the low‑µM range up to about 1 mM to provide sufficient data points for kinetic modelling.

steps.title: Prepare negative controls
steps.instruction: Mix the selected substrate stock solutions with HEPES buffer to obtain the same concentrations as in the test wells, fill one plate row (row G) with 200 µL per well (100 µL substrate mixture + 100 µL HEPES).

steps.title: Add diluted sludge to assay wells
steps.instruction: Using an 8‑channel pipette, dispense 100 µL of the diluted sludge suspension into each well of at least four rows. Verify that the suspension is stable and free of settled flocs before pipetting.

steps.title: Pre‑warm plate
steps.instruction: Place the plate on the carrier, insert into the measurement chamber and equilibrate at 30 °C for 10 min.

steps.title: Prepare calibration standards
steps.instruction: For two parallel calibration sets, prepare five 4‑MUF concentrations plus a blank. In each well, add buffer and 4‑MUF stock volumes that sum to 100 µL, add 100 µL HEPES to blanks, then add 100 µL prediluted sludge suspension (total 200 µL). Typical calibration range: 1.0–10.0 µM/L 4‑MUF (0.20–2.0 nmol per well).

steps.title: Add substrate to assay wells
steps.instruction: Without delay, add 100 µL of each pre‑heated (30 °C) substrate solution to the wells that already contain 100 µL diluted sludge (rows other than the negative‑control row).

steps.title: Run kinetic fluorescence read
steps.instruction: Immediately place the plate into the reader and start the kinetic program: total 15 min with fluorescence measurements every 90 s.

steps.title: Transform raw fluorescence data
steps.instruction: Transfer RFU data to Excel (or similar). Compute means for each pair of kinetic replicates and for the two calibration replicates. Subtract the mean RFU of the negative controls from each test replicate with the same substrate concentration at each time point. For each measurement interval, generate a linear calibration function from the duplicate calibration means, convert RFU to 4‑MUF concentration (µM/L) and then to amount (nmol/well) by dividing by 5. Apply the calibration to sample RFU values. Subtract the 4‑MUF amount at time zero from all later readings (if subtraction yields a negative value, add that offset to all readings).

steps.title: Convert to original sludge concentration
steps.instruction: Multiply the corrected 4‑MUF / well values by the sludge dilution factor and by the reciprocal of the sludge volume added to the well (0.1 mL). Example: dilution factor = 5, sludge volume = 0.1 mL → overall factor = 5 ÷ 0.1 = 50.

steps.title: Calculate reaction rates
steps.instruction: For each initial substrate concentration, perform linear regression of 4‑MUF amount (nmol) versus time (min) to obtain the slope (nmol · mL⁻¹ · min⁻¹, i.e., mU/mL). Record the coefficient of determination (R²) to assess linearity.

steps.title: Determine Michaelis‑Menten parameters
steps.instruction: Fit the set of reaction rates versus initial substrate concentrations by nonlinear regression (e.g., Excel Solver) to obtain K_M (µM) and V_max (nmol · mL⁻¹ · min⁻¹).

steps.title: Inhibitor fluorescence check
steps.instruction: Ensure the chosen inhibitor does not fluoresce in the 4‑MUF emission range and does not alter 4‑MUF‑P or 4‑MUF fluorescence. Verify solubility at the assay pH.

steps.title: Add inhibitor to controls and standards
steps.instruction: In negative‑control and calibration wells, add 50 µL of a four‑fold concentrated inhibitor solution (step 7 & 10 modification). Adjust substrate and 4‑MUF‑P dosing volumes to 50 µL each (total 100 µL) and double the substrate concentration accordingly. If prior tests show no fluorescence effect, this modification is optional.

steps.title: Add inhibitor to assay wells
steps.instruction: Immediately before substrate addition (step 11), dispense 50 µL of the inhibitor solution into each assay well, then add 50 µL of the substrate solution (double concentration) to maintain a total of 100 µL substrate‑plus‑inhibitor mixture.

steps.title: Design inhibition plate layout
steps.instruction: Use at least two 96‑well plates. Example layout: Plate 1 – rows A‑C: sludge + substrate (no inhibitor); rows D‑F: sludge + substrate + inhibitor X (e.g., 5 µM tungstate); row G: negative controls; row H: wells 1‑6 calibration standards without inhibitor, wells 7‑12 calibration standards with inhibitor X. Plate 2 – rows A‑C: sludge + substrate + inhibitor Y (e.g., 25 µM); rows D‑F: sludge + substrate + inhibitor Z (e.g., 100 µM); row G: negative controls; row H: calibration standards with inhibitors Y and Z as above. Three replicates per condition are required.

steps.title: Analyze inhibition kinetics
steps.instruction: Process the data as in steps 13‑16 to obtain apparent K′_M and V′_max for each inhibitor concentration. Compare how these parameters change with inhibitor level to infer the inhibition mechanism (e.g., competitive, non‑competitive) using plots or software such as GraphPad Prism or SigmaPlot.
